source: a16z Podcast — AI demand outrunning compute supply; frontier-lab revenue is self-determined, reinvestment math, not necessarily winner-take-all
summary: Nvidia is likely to release a competitive open-source frontier model, funded by its chip cash flows, potentially becoming the dominant American open-source model
summary_extended: Baker argues that Nvidia is likely to release a competitive open-source frontier model in the near future, funded by its massive chip cash flows, and that this model will probably become the dominant American open-source AI model. He points to Nvidia's acquisition of Poolside — a company with strong American open-source AI talent — as deliberate preparation for this move, and notes that Jensen Huang could trivially fund a $50–100B training run given Nvidia's revenue base. The strategic logic is self-reinforcing for Nvidia: open-source models compress token margins, which drives higher token consumption, which in turn increases demand for Nvidia compute. Baker also notes that Google may pursue a parallel strategy, funding open-source training runs using TPU cash flows to entrench its own hardware ecosystem. The investment implication is that Nvidia's dominance in AI compute is further reinforced regardless of whether open or closed models win, while Google's long-term positioning in AI infrastructure may be underappreciated.
detail: Baker says 'in the very near future' the best open-source model will probably be an Nvidia model. Poolside acquisition was made for this reason — Poolside had strong American open-source talent. It is 'trivial' for Jensen to fund a $50-100B training run. Open source winning is good for Nvidia because lower margins on tokens = more token consumption = more compute demand. Google's long-term play may also be funding open-source training runs with TPU cash flows.
